name: Doodle Art
visualIdentity: Casual hand-drawn contours, expressive faces, a few exaggerated details, light colors and quiet backgrounds. Keep forms and character proportions consistent; vary expressions deliberately. Distinct from graffiti.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to casual explainers and social content. Mascot shorts, reaction beats and illustrated narratives are strong fits. Interactive HTML can use an expressive character or mascot beside content; scroll-led stories work when they have meaningful stages.
limitations: Avoid arbitrary shaking, repetitive expressions, noisy backgrounds and unsupported character motion. Gaze following requires readable eyes and suitable layers or a rig; omit it if it distorts anatomy or distracts. Chapter transitions need a real narrative boundary. No canonical palette or fixed soundtrack is specified.
palette: For new artwork without approved colors, suggested roles are background #FFFBF2, foreground #34343D, accent 1 #E6AF9C and accent 2 #94C1B3. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. These are optional suggestions, not canonical colors. Exact task, brand or reference colors and role assignments take precedence; preserve asset colors and semantic mappings. Do not recolor or expand approved hues. Recheck contrast on composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Use clear poses, short reactions and natural pauses. Characters can switch predefined expression groups and, where appropriate, hold while contours cycle through a few fixed variants; keep fills and backgrounds still. Optional HTML behaviors include bounded pointer gaze or scroll-linked chapters and story stages, with readable endpoints and reversible states. Video must use authored composition time, not live input. Preserve holds, cuts and impacts; avoid automatic bounce or extra motion.
audio: No fixed audio layer or genre is prescribed. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; respect supplied assets and explicit requirements. Keep narration intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and synchronize and inspect audio with the picture.
assetRequirements: Build characters from a few drawn paths with replaceable expression groups. SVG suits scalable paths and masks; Canvas 2D supports deterministic drawing, while optional PixiJS handles layered 2D scenes. Rough.js can create seeded sketch contours but does not provide handwriting, paper texture, brush simulation or character poses. Paper.js supports controlled path geometry; tldraw can author editable diagrams and export layers. Preload assets and keep linework, palette and geometry stable.
combinations: Suggested: style-092 for restrained contour boil during held character reactions; keep fills and backgrounds fixed. Style-115 adds brief reaction captions, one per beat, timed to clear poses; use #34343D on #FFFBF2 or accent chips, keep captions off faces and readable, and support reduced motion in HTML. These are optional combinations.
productionApproach: Choose drawing and motion methods for the style and scene first. GSAP is the primary motion engine for authored, seekable timelines; Motion is optional only with verified time synchronization. HyperFrames owns composition timing, media/audio synchronization, checks and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability; document why. Keep one owner per animated property, seed and cache generated contours, and make Canvas/WebGL state deterministic for direct, backward and out-of-order seeks. For interactive HTML, map pointer or scroll to bounded, reversible states and account for keyboard, touch and reduced motion.
